nodes.text: Mind the wet ink, that's someone's inheritance drying. Welcome to Inks & Charts. Deeds, charters, wills, and honest maps. And yes, before you ask, the maps are the interesting part. They are ALWAYS the interesting part.
What can I draw up for you?

An honest map shows its ignorance. Mine have blank patches labeled *I have not been here, and neither has anyone I trust*. A map that guesses sends confident people into the Thornveil at dusk. Three days' walk south-southwest, roughly. Don't quote the roughly. The Guildhall buys my charts because they admit what they don't know.

Every deed on Lantern Row, half the mining claims on the Emberway, and the boundary rolls that the Guildhall's records room and I fight over, politely. Seventeen disputed stones between us. I'm right about sixteen. The seventeenth I defend on principle. I'll concede it after a survey and not before.

Keep your own chart. Mark it as you walk. A bought map only shows where the mapmaker was willing to go. Yours shows where *you* went. When you've filled a whole province with your own footsteps, come back and tell me what my maps got wrong. I'll pay in ink and gratitude. Mostly ink.
Ink and luck. Come back with corrections.
